summary: Idle client connections holding GPU slots -> slot leasing leak and gradual throughput drain on Dedicated pool
description: Customer reports a slow, progressive drop in dedicated-pool throughput starting ~2026-03-11 10:00 UTC. P50 throughput steady but p99 and overall throughput have trended down over 8-12 hours, despite no recorded GPU driver errors. Symptoms looked like a noisy-neighbor allocation issue but was reproducible only under the customer's traffic pattern. Attach: dashboard snapshots, allocator logs. Impact: customer observed ~30% lower completed inference requests/hour on reserved pool; some requests hit autoscaler fallbacks to shared capacity.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs sustained short-lived chat requests (median context 256 tokens, request duration 100-300ms) with a 5s keepalive between streams.
2) Traffic pattern has many clients opening long-lived HTTP/2 streams but not sending traffic continuously (idle connections with periodic pings).
3) Over several hours, dedicated pool p50 stable but total active GPU slot count drops and request queueing increases; autoscaler triggers fallback routing.
logs: sidecar-proxy: connection id=conn-192.168.10.5 state=IDLE last_active=2026-03-11T11:02:17Z keepalive=5s
investigation: Initial hypothesis: noisy tenant or heavy mini-bursts causing allocator to fragment slots. Dashboards did not show typical short streaming fanout spikes.

Observed: a subset of customer-side connections held GPU leases far longer than request duration. Leases show TTLs ~1h with no active inference traffic for many minutes, preventing reuse and reducing effective pool capacity.

Recreated pattern in staging by simulating many clients opening streams and retaining them idle with 5s TCP/TLS-level keepalives. Staging reproduced gradual drop in available active slots similar to prod.

Root cause: customer SDK (v1.x) behavior opened a persistent sidecar connection per logical user/session and performed aggressive keepalives that prevented the sidecar and allocator from detecting inactive leases. The serving runtime treats the connection as in-use while the sidecar held the slot, which effectively leaked slot capacity under high connection cardinality.

Contributing factor: allocator TTL/idle-detection thresholds were conservative to avoid evicting legitimately long-running sessions; this interacted poorly with the customer's pattern of many short requests with long-lived idle connections.
comments: 2026-03-12 Priya Desai: Triage complete; escalated to SRE for memory/driver checks. Customer reports 30% throughput loss. Requesting allocator logs + sample connection IDs.

2026-03-12 Evan Park: Found many 'leased' slots with last_active timestamps >30m. Pushing a staging repro plan and short-term mitigations. Opening INT ticket to adjust allocator idle-detection in a canary.
2026-03-12 MapWise Support (customer): We don't see errors on our side; SDK keeps a session per user and uses connection pings every 5s for NAT traversal. We can try a client change if recommended.

2026-03-13 SRE (J. Morales): Canary patch prepared to add a heuristic: if connection has held a slot and no inference RPCs have been issued for >120s, mark slot eligible for preemptive release (controlled by feature flag).

2026-03-13 Priya Desai: Customer applied SDK patch candidate (2.1.3-beta) that reuses connection pools and switched keepalive to 30s on a subset of traffic; initial pilot shows recovered throughput +20% within 30 minutes.
resolution_notes: - Short-term: instruct customer to upgrade SDK to >=2.1.3 (beta) which enables connection pooling and extends keepalive interval (recommended 30s) which prevented slot leaks in our repro.

- Platform-side: deployed canary allocator heuristic (feature flag: allocator.idle_preempt=true) in us-east dedicated cluster. Heuristic frees slots with no active RPCs for >120s even if connection remains open.
- Engineering to land PR to sidecar-proxy (PR #412) to surface protocol-level idle signals so allocator can detect true inactivity without relying on TTL only.
- Update dedicated-pool runbook: add 'idle-connection leak' section and a dashboard for idle_slot_ratio and per-tenant connection_cardinality.
- Outreach: coordinate with MapWise to fully roll out SDK change and validate production stability over 72h window.
Status: partial workaround in prod canary (us-east) and customer pilot successful. Remaining: full sidecar change and allocator tuning across regions.
